za-0BuS.title: Road: grainy pavement with a pink tint
za-0BuS.summary: A grainy, almost Texas-like road surface with a hint of pink, found in the far north-east.

za-2WI6.title: Road lines: white triple centre line
za-2WI6.summary: Sometimes a triple centre line: two solid white lines with a dashed one inside. Another version has two white lines with a yellow one in the middle, usually on big main roads. Only the neighbouring southern African countries have these.

za-58eY.title: Crops: sugarcane along the east coast
za-58eY.summary: Sugarcane plantations are most common on the east coast, and also on the north-east border in another province.

za-7cr3.title: Poles: stuck-on adverts for abortion and enlargement pills
za-7cr3.summary: Poles and public property are often covered in dodgy adverts for abortion services or enlargement pills, in and around the northern urban area, especially the biggest city and one mining town.

za-Btnv.title: Road lines: yellow edges, white centre
za-Btnv.summary: Single yellow lines at the road edge and white lines in the middle. Botswana, Eswatini, Lesotho and Namibia use them too. Australia practically never uses yellow edge lines.

differs.how: Practically never has yellow edge lines

za-D9sE.title: Pole: 1 or 2 metal arms holding insulators
za-D9sE.summary: Poles with one or two metal arms are most common in the east, in one inland province.

za-EHXL.title: Landscape: flat savannah, grass and small trees, waystones
za-EHXL.summary: Around the big north-east park: flat, dry savannah with grass, scattered small trees, red soil, and distinctive direction waystones at junctions. Mostly gravel roads or small unmarked paved roads.

za-EW6K.title: Plants: very tall Cook pines on the south-east coast
za-EW6K.summary: Tall Cook pines grow mostly between two south-east coast cities. They are planted, so they can appear anywhere on the coast.

za-Fho0.title: Pole: two diagonal bars forming a < shape
za-Fho0.summary: Poles with 2 diagonal bars forming a < shape are mostly in the north-east, most often in the far north and the north-west.

za-G6kZ.title: Landscape: mountains visible north of a southern city
za-G6kZ.summary: Mountains in a nature reserve, likely a peak named after a man, are visible north of the southern coastal city.

za-GgUS.title: Landscape: dry, barren, orange-red soil, shrub hills
za-GgUS.summary: The north-east can look very dry and barren, with orange or red soil and hills covered in shrubs. Coverage can change from dry to very green depending on season.

za-Hx3k.title: Sign: triangular warning sign, red border
za-Hx3k.summary: Warning signs are red-bordered triangles on white. The other southern African countries use similar ones. Australia and New Zealand use yellow diamonds.

za-IPzM.title: Sign: M route signs in two coastal cities
za-IPzM.summary: Metropolitan routes, big roads around cities, carry the letter M. The sign designs are distinct in one south-east port city and in the east coast city.

za-ISiU.title: Pole: three strips of reflective tape on signal poles
za-ISiU.summary: In the biggest northern city, traffic light and crossing poles have three strips of reflective tape around them.

za-KDMw.title: Pole: 3 alternating insulators sticking out sideways
za-KDMw.summary: Poles with 3 alternating insulators sticking out horizontally are mostly in the four northern provinces, sometimes the north-west dry region. Very rare elsewhere.

za-LxHT.title: Language: English plus Afrikaans place names
za-LxHT.summary: English is most common on signs. Afrikaans looks like Dutch, with place name endings like -fontein, -kraal, -kop, -dorp, -nek and -berg. It appears nationwide, so it does not help pick a region.

za-OMTa.title: Road: reddish asphalt, dry grey trees, golden grass
za-OMTa.summary: On one road north of a border village next to Botswana, reddish-tinted asphalt, arid land with grey dry trees, shrubs and long golden grass. The road runs north-south. Red asphalt also appears elsewhere, but this landscape is typical here.

za-OmMx.title: Sign: three-digit R roads grouped by region
za-OmMx.summary: Most three-digit R roads are geographically grouped, but many cross provinces and the 100s are spread across the whole country. The map shows roughly where each set is.

za-Oy3D.title: Pole: big bird nests on top
za-Oy3D.summary: Big bird nests sit on top of poles, commonly in the northern part of the dry north-west province.

za-Prjw.title: Pole: wide A-shaped top, insulators on the A
za-Prjw.summary: Similar A-shape but noticeably wider, with the bottom insulators attached directly to the A instead of a horizontal bar. Found in the south-east.

za-Q1UD.title: Landscape: dry land with red soil, north-west
za-Q1UD.summary: A dry landscape with red soil is typical of the north-west province. The climate map is a useful guide.

za-RWlO.title: Pole: trident pole tops
za-RWlO.summary: Trident pole tops are almost unique to the east coast province.

za-ShVC.title: Houses: high walls, fences and gates
za-ShVC.summary: Suburban houses in and around big cities are often surrounded by high walls, fences and gates.

za-UBPX.title: Landscape: rocky treeless mountains, steep sides
za-UBPX.summary: Rocky, treeless mountains with tall steep sides and sharp peaks in the south-west. Similar mountains are in and around Lesotho.

za-Ud2I.title: Chevron: white-and-red, plus thin single-arrow ones
za-Ud2I.summary: White-and-red chevrons, with the same pattern under direction signs. Small thin single-arrow chevrons by the road are common, and neighbouring southern African countries have them too.

za-UxL1.title: Pole: narrow A-shaped top on a horizontal bar
za-UxL1.summary: Poles with 3 bars forming an A, with the bottom insulators on the ends of a horizontal bar. Almost only in the south-west, rarely in neighbouring provinces.

za-VsjT.title: Street lamp: arm with a bump on top
za-VsjT.summary: This lamp and arm shows up rarely across the country, but one east coast city has a bump on top. You may still see the standard lamp.

za-Z6GT.title: Google car: camouflage car, black mirrors, roof racks
za-Z6GT.summary: In the big north-east national park, a camouflage car with black side mirrors and roof racks. The park also has Gen 4 coverage now.

za-bF5N.title: Google car: Gen 2, big round blur, sky halo
za-bF5N.summary: Gen 2 is fairly common. It has a big round blur where the car is and a halo-like colour glow in the sky. In Africa, only this country has Gen 2.

za-eJUt.title: Sign: white stickers on chevron backs
za-eJUt.summary: White stickers on the back of chevrons are often seen in the Cape provinces in the south and west.

za-iJbI.title: Landscape: power plants between two towns
za-iJbI.summary: Power plants appear between two towns in the east inland province.

za-iZzK.title: Plate: each province has its own design
za-iZzK.summary: Plate designs differ by province and may show through the blur. Two stand out: one has a slight green tint, another a blue tint.

za-jfTY.title: Google car: Gen 4 smallcam, low with big blur
za-jfTY.summary: A Gen 4 camera mounted lower than normal, with a big round blur and a small bump at the front. The blur can be see-through, but a short antenna shows at the back.

za-lm-411.title: Google car: blue back means this country or Europe
za-lm-411.summary: A blue car back, with or without an antenna, means you are in this country or Europe. Add yellow edge lines and driving on the left, and it can only be here.

za-lm-7828.title: Road lines: yellow edges, white centre vs Australia
za-lm-7828.summary: Most paved roads have single yellow edge lines and white centre lines. Australia only has white. Middle Eastern countries can have yellow edges too, so check driving side. Botswana, Eswatini and Lesotho share them but usually have a white car.

differs.how: Only white lines, never single yellow

za-lm-870.title: Landscape: yellow boulders scattered around
za-lm-870.summary: In the north, north-east of the main city, big yellow boulders lie around as if a giant dropped his toys.

za-mWX6.title: Plants: pine plantations next to the western border
za-mWX6.summary: Tree plantations that are mostly pine are common west of Eswatini and in some parts of the east coast province to the south. Pine plantations are normally seen inside Eswatini itself.

za-nLmo.title: Driving side: left
za-nLmo.summary: Traffic drives on the left. A handful of other countries do too.

za-nSzl.title: Crops: vineyards in coastal valleys
za-nSzl.summary: Vineyards are almost only in the south-west, mostly in coastal valleys. They also appear near one inland town in the north-west.

za-p5p1.title: Landscape: flat and green subtropical near the border
za-p5p1.summary: Near the north-east border with Mozambique the land is noticeably flat with green subtropical plants.

za-pE0c.title: Sign: N before the number, blue pentagon on maps
za-pE0c.summary: On road signs the highway number has an N in front. On Google Maps the N is missing and a blue pentagon with the number is shown instead.

za-pn0o.title: Phone numbers: 10 digits, area code starts with 0
za-pn0o.summary: Numbers are 10 digits. Landlines start with a 0 followed by two digits for the area, and areas are geographically grouped. Mobile numbers start with 06 to 08 and say nothing about area.

za-riHx.title: Pole: bird poles, white insulators on bars
za-riHx.summary: The most common pole has 1 to 5 horizontal bars with thin white insulators that look like rows of birds. Many other pole types exist, some limited to certain regions.

za-t7mv.title: Landscape: flat-topped mountain with pyramid neighbour
za-t7mv.summary: A famous mountain west of the main southern city with a 3 km flat plateau, flanked by a more pyramid-shaped peak.

za-u08Z.title: Sign: square red stickers on sign backs
za-u08Z.summary: Square red stickers on the back of regular signs are common in the south-east and close to it in the dry north-west and the centre. A little in the north-west. Red stickers on chevron backs appear in almost every province.

za-ulWW.title: Google car: Gen 4 blue car, short antenna
za-ulWW.summary: All Gen 4 coverage shows a blue car with a short antenna. The blur sometimes hides the antenna.

za-wMNA.title: Landscape: grassy rolling hills, ridges north or east
za-wMNA.summary: Grassy rolling hills on the south-west coast between the main city and a southern town, and just north of the city. Tall ridges usually appear to the north or east.

za-x5Nk.title: Sign: green direction sign, yellow road number
za-x5Nk.summary: Green direction signs with a yellow road number. Neighbours use the same, so read the number: N and R roads exist only here, A and B roads in Botswana, Lesotho and Namibia, and MR roads in Eswatini.
